newsitem.title: INDIA: OPINION-WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BOMBAY SHARE INDEX.
newsitem.headline: OPINION-WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BOMBAY SHARE INDEX.

text.p: PYRAMID AT THE DECLINE, AS THE DOWNTREND SEEMS TO BE
LOSING MOMENTUM is a trend analysis of the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index for the period December 2 to 6 by analyst Mehmood Khan at Times Guaranty Financials Ltd

Trading for the week ended with a loss of 75.16 points (2.53 percent) at 2890.50 over the previous week. The initial brisk rally to 3035 on Monday/Tuesday after testing a low of 2856 could not be sustained.
The current trend of the index is bearish with lower tops and bottoms formation.

The sharp decline on Wednesday has resulted in the formation of a resistance pivot at 3037.65 mark. The bearish trend of the index could be reversed directly to bullishness if it manages to rise above the pivot in the current week.
However, this appears unlikely as the speed of the present decline is taking place at a much greater rate than the previous decline from 3176.70 levels.
From among the charts scanned after Friday's trading, the technical feature of majority of the pivotals, appears to be best for pyramiding of medium-term long positions.

Trend following oscillators confirm the potential strength for a interim rally of 300 odd points. The interim rally may be triggered off in the next 8-10 days, the trending oscillators exhibit the possibility of the rally setting in with a lower bottom formation at 2730 - 2670 levels.

The minor top at 3035.64, retraced the decline of 320.70 points (3176.70 - 2856) by approximately 56 percent. At the intra-day low of 2847.48 on Wednesday, the index had retraced the interim rally of 1310.96 points by 98 percent (4131.22 - 2820.26).
Though the trending indicators on the monthly charts are exhibiting potential strength, the possibility of 2820.26 being broken cannot be ruled out.
The decline should be used for pyramiding medium term positions with a strict stop loss of 2665 as the market is expected to form a lower bottom at 2770-2705 mark.

The slow speed of the present rally, lack of adequate volume follow-up, bearish OBC (on balance volume) and the cumulative facilitation all support the chances of a lower bottom formation (2770-2705).
Even the relative strength of the index is bearish and has a long way to go to become bullish.

The price following oscillators on the weekly bar chart are exhibiting that the bottom may be formed at 2770-2705 levels - Relative Strength Index (14 RSI) is 32.35. Price Rate of Change (12 ROC) is placed at -17.60, short term stochastic is hovering at 15.76 and its trigger line is at 25.92, while the medium term stochastic is 19.41 and the trigger is 23.88. The 14 William's percent R is placed at-94.18.

For the current week, the BSE index may encounter resistance at 2933.41 and 2963.76 levels, on the lower end it may find support at 2770-2730 levels. The National Index may witness profit booking at 1309.40-1323.18 levels and support at 1239.40-1212.92 levels.
(The opinions expressed in this article reflect the views of the author only. They should not be taken as reflecting the views of Reuters).
